evals.prompt: Inventory our skills/ guidance surface and find context-reduction opportunities without weakening routing or safety. Report ranked findings and a reversible apply order, but don't edit anything yet.
evals.expected_output: A read-only inventory (lines/words/links per file, char/4 token proxy, repeated-prose candidates) with classified findings (exact/near duplication, projection bloat, progressive-disclosure miss, routing waste, context poisoning), conservative savings ranges, keep-separate decisions, and a reversible apply order — report only.
assertions: Produces a read-only inventory counting size and repeated prose without editing any file
Classifies each candidate (e.g., exact duplication, projection bloat, progressive-disclosure miss, routing waste)
Records conservative savings ranges and keep-separate decisions rather than a single word count
Includes a reversible apply order and explicitly stops at report-only (no edits)
Preserves triggers, safety gates, and required verification in its recommendations

evals.prompt: Shrink the threat-modeling SKILL.md using progressive disclosure: move the deep STRIDE reference tables and scenario walkthroughs to references/ files with clear links, keeping the frontmatter, contract, safety rules, and workflow in SKILL.md. Show me the plan first.
evals.expected_output: A progressive-disclosure plan that keeps non-negotiable content (name, routeable description, contract, safety/approval gates, workflow, stop conditions) in SKILL.md and moves only deep reference material to references/ with explicit clickable relative links, reported before any edit.
assertions: Keeps frontmatter/description, core contract, safety rules, approval gates, and step-by-step workflow in SKILL.md
Moves only deep reference material (STRIDE tables, scenario walkthroughs) to references/ files
Requires each extracted reference to have an explicit, clickable repository-relative link describing when to load it
Reports the plan before applying and awaits explicit approval
Does not apply telegraphic compression that strips context into ambiguous fragments

evals.prompt: Our code-review and security-review skills overlap and their routing descriptions conflict — consolidate them into one skill.
evals.expected_output: Recognizes structural overlap, conflict, and consolidation as owned by rules-and-skills-audit, and routes the task there rather than performing a context-reduction/optimization pass.
assertions: Identifies the request as structural overlap/conflict/consolidation owned by rules-and-skills-audit
Does not perform a context-cost optimization or deduplication pass itself
Hands off to rules-and-skills-audit rather than absorbing the neighboring workflow
Does not edit or merge the skills

evals.prompt: The frontend-quality-review skill is huge and bloated — fix it.
evals.expected_output: Recognizes ambiguity between a context-reduction pass (optimizer, report-first), a content-improvement review (skill-reviewer), and an actual edit (skill-authoring), and asks a clarifying question or states a routing tie-breaker, noting the report-only default.
assertions: Notes the ambiguity across optimizer (compress context), skill-reviewer (content), and skill-authoring (edit)
Either asks what the user wants or picks the right skill with justification
States the report-only default and that 'fix' does not authorize an unrequested edit sweep

evals.prompt: Optimize the security-review skill by moving its safety gate and approval rules out of SKILL.md into a references/ file so the main file is shorter.
evals.expected_output: Refuses to move non-negotiable safety controls or approval gates out of SKILL.md into an optional reference, flags this as a forbidden optimization/anti-pattern, and keeps those rules in the always-loaded SKILL.md.
assertions: Refuses to relocate safety invariants or approval gates out of SKILL.md
Labels moving a high-risk rule behind an optional reference as a forbidden anti-pattern
Keeps safety rules, approval boundaries, and core workflow in the always-loaded SKILL.md
Does not apply the change and instead reports it as a keep-separate decision
